solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brief picture of biscuits burning

parts.note: ginger snaps are crisp biscuits, so snaps can mean biscuits
something burning is hot

explanation.surface: A cook sees a plate of biscuits catching fire and describes the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick, informal photograph, a brief picture taken in an instant.

clue.text: Crab? Silly oaf does

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are jumbled foolishly into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool behaves like a crab, a silly thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Crab as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab is one example of seafood, edible creatures from the sea.

clue.text: I will briefly broadcast in passageway

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, so the contraction is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: I will shortened is the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: Someone promises to make a short radio announcement in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: Sign I'd led men astray with just one purpose

indicators.note: astray means gone wrong or off course, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A misleading signpost sent a group of men the wrong way, apparently on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-minded means wholly focused on one aim or goal, determined.

clue.text: Own goal to include Republican article in periodical

indicators.note: to include says the first piece takes the next one inside it

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A magazine features a piece about a political own goal involving a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or magazine serving as the mouthpiece of a group.

clue.text: Highly curious in past, prying ultimately

parts.note: something in the past happened long ago

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word prying

explanation.surface: Someone has been nosy about another person's history and is eager to hear more.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes eager excitement and curiosity, wanting badly to know what happens.

clue.text: Romeo's lass cut top off plant

parts.note: a gal is a girl or lass

indicators.note: cut top off says the first letter of plant is removed, top being the start in a down clue

explanation.surface: Romeo's girlfriend prunes the head off a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is an attentive ladies' man, which is what a Romeo is.

clue.text: Rating turned colour of ash, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: something that has turned ash-coloured has greyed

explanation.surface: A sailor went pale as ash, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a sailor, but means a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a rank or level awarded, which is a rating.

clue.text: Satiric actor affectedly upper-class?

indicators.note: affectedly suggests the letters are put on in an artificial, rearranged way

explanation.surface: A comic performer puts on airs, mimicking the posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocratic means belonging to the nobility, the highest social class.

clue.text: Clergyman forgetting first offence

indicators.note: forgetting first says the opening letter of the clergyman word is dropped

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A forgetful vicar has committed his first wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Go by stream with a fierce guy

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Someone walks past a brook alongside an aggressive man.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is slang for a big, brutish thug or heavy, a fierce man.

clue.text: Just starting old Danish epic poem

indicators.note: just starting means only the opening letters of the next three words are kept

explanation.surface: A long ancient Scandinavian narrative verse, like Beowulf, is only getting under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb of time but works with 'starting' to say only initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, usually addressed to a subject in an elevated style.

clue.text: Wins top English painting

parts.note: to land a prize or contract is to win it
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: An English artwork takes first prize in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture depicting a scene of countryside, a genre of painting.

clue.text: Energetic guy from Soho many dearly recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Many people in London's Soho fondly remember a lively man.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden word: 'from' marks the stretch sOHO MANY Dearly, and 'recalled' turns it round. Soho is a London entertainment district.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a forceful, tirelessly active person, named after the electricity generator.

clue.text: Figure meal run out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner works out the cost of a meal that has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a symbol for a number, a figure such as 7 or VII.

clue.text: Linger and look into Ebro, oddly

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words into Ebro

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles while gazing at the Spanish river Ebro.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about idly, which is to linger.

clue.text: Regret referring to signalling code

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
Morse is the dot-and-dash signalling code

explanation.surface: Someone apologises about a message sent in a telegraph code.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret or guilt for a wrong done.

clue.text: Room at inn organised for one proposing candidate

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A room at an inn has been booked for someone putting forward a candidate in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominator is a person who puts someone forward for election or office.

clue.text: Unpleasant refusal to accommodate street

indicators.note: to accommodate says the first piece houses the second inside it

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal

explanation.surface: A disagreeable council turns down a request to house a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means disagreeable or offensive, the same as unpleasant.

clue.text: Complete stop as outsiders leave — speech unfinished

indicators.note: as outsiders leave says the first and last letters of stop go, keeping the inner pair
unfinished says the speech word loses its last letter

parts.note: a talk is a speech

explanation.surface: A lecturer halts as people walk out, leaving the address incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Total, as an adjective, means complete or absolute, as in total silence.

clue.text: Faded image partly indistinct

indicators.note: partly says only part of the words Faded image is used, letters spanning both

explanation.surface: An old photograph has faded, leaving its picture somewhat blurred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faded' looks like the definition, but the answer is hidden across 'fadeD IMage'; 'indistinct' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim means faint or poorly lit, hence hard to make out or indistinct.

clue.text: Boxer maybe supported by mother's belief

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A fighter holds firm convictions, backed by his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter; it is the dog breed, with 'maybe' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down as undeniably true, a firmly held belief.

clue.text: Too much foam from waves — draw back

parts.note: surf is the foam of breaking waves

indicators.note: back says the word for a draw is read in reverse

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: A swimmer, faced with too much spray from the breakers, retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw back' reads as retreat, but 'draw' gives TIE and 'back' turns it to EIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an amount that is more than enough.

clue.text: Cat, it's returned with good Queen

indicators.note: returned says the word it is written backwards

parts.note: it's is read as it is, the word it
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A pet cat has come back home with a well-behaved monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family.

clue.text: Cowardly, ignoring old wife's shout

indicators.note: ignoring says the old wife letters are left out of the coward word

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly
OW, old wife, from O for old and W for wife

explanation.surface: A timid man pays no attention to his elderly spouse's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud cry, a shout.

clue.text: We hear group of countries support barrier

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a bloc is a group of countries allied together; aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Listeners learn that an alliance of nations is backing a barricade.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockade is an obstruction sealing off a place, so it acts as a barrier.
